propositions: Newly added hard-fail CI gates broke four in-flight branches (medium-loved-newt, impudent-sodium-ferret, rancid-aerophobic-skylark, brattish-ladyish-jaguar) because code-review gate had no criterion checking whether a branch created before a pipeline change would now fail.
Escaped-bug analysis identified regression pattern: ungrandfathered gates land review-clean without checking compatibility with pre-existing branches.

Proposed solution is an advisory code-review criterion (project.ci-gate-compat) that evaluates whether pipeline/gate-configuration changes introduce hard-fail steps or required gates lacking grandfather guards, phrased CI-agnostically to support any CI vendor.

Criterion must trigger declaratively via applies_to glob seam (not hard-coded vendor paths) across eight CI systems to maintain portability and allow projects to override globs via [code_review] ci_config_globs config key.
Implementation requires gating project criteria dispatch on their applies_to globs against changed files, filtering activated criteria in gate_dispatch.py and registry.py.
